name: New York
note: Configuration for nyc.html (the same engine as chicago.html). The geography comes from OpenStreetMap via tools/fetch-osm.py nyc and tools/build-osm-city.py nyc into nyc-osm.json. The map is Manhattan from the Battery to the north end of Central Park, with the Hudson and East Rivers either side. This file holds the districts, landmark decorations, detailed street areas and viewpoints. Positions are [lat, lon].

fetch._: bbox and tiles for tools/fetch-osm.py; detailZones for tools/build-osm-city.py. Manhattan's water is tidal, so OSM maps its shores as natural=coastline and the build script takes the land from those rings.

terrain._: elevation grid spacing in metres; tiles from tools/fetch-terrain.py

districts._: [name, hex colour, base height, tallest, box as [lat south, lon west, lat north, lon east]]

el._: the subway is underground; the elevated stage draws only what OSM marks as elevated rail

landmarks.name: Empire State Building
landmarks.info: 350 Fifth Avenue · 1931 · 381 m to the roof, 443 m to the tip. Art deco, built in 410 days, and the tallest building in the world for 40 years.

landmarks.name: Chrysler Building
landmarks.info: 405 Lexington Avenue · 1930 · 319 m. The stainless steel crown and its arches, and the spire that was assembled in secret inside the building to beat 40 Wall Street.

landmarks.name: One World Trade Center
landmarks.info: 285 Fulton Street · 2014 · 417 m to the roof, 541 m to the tip — 1,776 feet. Eight tapering triangles on a cube base.

landmarks.name: 432 Park Avenue
landmarks.info: 2015 · 426 m of square concrete grid, 1:15 slenderness. The one that started the pencil towers.

landmarks.name: One Vanderbilt
landmarks.info: 2020 · 427 m, next to Grand Central, with four tapering facets angled to the terminal.

landmarks.name: Steinway Tower
landmarks.info: 2021 · 435 m and only 18 m wide: the most slender skyscraper in the world.

landmarks.name: Central Park Tower
landmarks.info: 2020 · 472 m, the tallest residential building in the world, cantilevered east over its neighbour.

landmarks.name: 30 Hudson Yards
landmarks.info: 2019 · 387 m, with the Edge observation deck jutting out of its 100th floor.

landmarks.name: The Vessel
landmarks.info: Hudson Yards · 2019 · Thomas Heatherwick's climbable lattice of 154 flights of stairs.

landmarks.name: Rockefeller Center
landmarks.info: 30 Rockefeller Plaza · 1933 · 259 m. The slab that taught American cities how to do a plaza.

landmarks.name: Grand Central Terminal
landmarks.info: 89 East 42nd Street · 1913 · the Beaux-Arts concourse, the celestial ceiling, and 44 platforms under it.

landmarks.name: MetLife Building
landmarks.info: 200 Park Avenue · 1963 · 246 m, built over the tracks and straight across the axis of Park Avenue.

landmarks.name: Flatiron Building
landmarks.info: 175 Fifth Avenue · 1902 · 87 m on a triangular lot where Broadway crosses Fifth.

landmarks.name: Seagram Building
landmarks.info: 375 Park Avenue · 1958 · Mies van der Rohe's bronze tower set back behind its own plaza.

landmarks.name: Woolworth Building
landmarks.info: 233 Broadway · 1913 · 241 m. The 'Cathedral of Commerce', tallest in the world until 1930.

landmarks.name: Times Square
landmarks.info: Where Broadway cuts Seventh Avenue. The bowtie of light that the rest of the grid does not have.

landmarks.name: Madison Square Garden
landmarks.info: 4 Pennsylvania Plaza · 1968 · the arena built on top of the ruins of Penn Station.

landmarks.name: Bryant Park
landmarks.info: Behind the New York Public Library, on top of its book stacks.

landmarks.name: Washington Square Arch
landmarks.info: Greenwich Village · 1892 · marble, at the foot of Fifth Avenue.

landmarks.name: United Nations Headquarters
landmarks.info: First Avenue at 46th · 1952 · the Secretariat slab, on land that is not technically the United States.

landmarks.name: Brooklyn Bridge
landmarks.info: 1883 · granite towers and steel cable, and the first way across the East River.

landmarks.name: Manhattan Bridge
landmarks.info: 1909 · the one the subway crosses, and the one you photograph from DUMBO.

landmarks.name: Williamsburg Bridge
landmarks.info: 1903 · all steel, no masonry, and the longest suspension span in the world when it opened.

landmarks.name: Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge
landmarks.info: 1909 · the cantilever to Queens, over Roosevelt Island.

landmarks.name: Central Park
landmarks.info: 843 acres · 1858 · Olmsted and Vaux, every rock and lake of it built on purpose.

landmarks.name: The High Line
landmarks.info: A freight viaduct from 1934, planted and reopened as a park in 2009.

landmarks.name: Statue of Liberty
landmarks.info: Liberty Island · 1886 · 93 m to the torch, on her pedestal, facing out to the harbour.

_seaLevelWater: Manhattan's shores are tidal coastline in OSM, so the box is flooded at sea level and the elevation grid draws the island
